bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Product portfolio concentration — Named by management as a risk category: 'Dependence on a limited number of products and therapeutic segments', with stated impact of 'exposure to market volatility, pricing pressure and fluctuations in demand affecting profitability'. Structurally relevant because the Company is among the world's largest Ibuprofen manufacturers and Ibuprofen alone contributes 34.43% of total turnover (BRSR LCA table), with Ethyl Acetate a further 33.66% — i.e. two molecules account for roughly two-thirds of revenue. Mitigation stated: portfolio diversification across APIs and specialty chemicals, supported by expansion into new products and markets (non-Ibuprofen APIs up from 18% in FY21 to 37% in FY26).
- Single-site / single-complex operational concentration and fire & industrial hazard exposure — All manufacturing is at one fully integrated complex at Barnala, Punjab (BRSR: 1 plant nationally, no international plants). Management flags 'Fire and Industrial Hazards' arising from fire incidents, equipment malfunction, unsafe conditions or process failures, with impact of damage to assets and infrastructure, production disruptions, financial losses and employee safety incidents. Any event at the single site would affect both the API and chemical divisions simultaneously. Mitigation: fire protection systems, periodic safety drills, awareness programmes, emergency response procedures, robust EHS systems, periodic audits and environmental monitoring.
- Occupational health & safety, including a fatality recorded in the year — Occupational Health & Safety, Emergency Preparedness and Safe Material Handling are all classified as Social RISK material topics, and the BRSR materiality table notes Health & Safety can 'directly impact people and community and disrupt the operations' with NEGATIVE financial implications. Materially, the BRSR safety table discloses 1 employee fatality and 1 total recordable work-related injury in FY 2025-26 against nil in FY 2024-25, with employee LTIFR rising from 0 to 1.46 per million person-hours — against a stated target of Zero Lost Time Fatality Rate. Mitigation: ISO 45001:2018-certified OHS management system covering 100% of plants and offices, HIRA/JSA/HAZOP/AIA/PSSR methodologies, an online Incident Prevention Opportunity (IPO) hazard-reporting portal, EHS training and periodic mock drills.
- Supply chain disruption and raw-material dependence — Root causes stated: dependence on key suppliers, logistics bottlenecks, geopolitical developments, natural disasters and equipment failures; impact stated as production interruptions, delayed deliveries, increased costs and revenue loss. Mitigation: supplier diversification, strategic inventory management, business continuity planning, cross-functional response mechanisms, and — structurally — backward integration across key intermediates including in-house Iso Butyl Benzene.
- Product quality variability and regulatory/compliance exposure — Classified as a Regulatory & Compliance risk. Root causes: process deviations, raw material inconsistencies, equipment issues and non-conformance to quality standards; impact: customer complaints, product recalls, regulatory action, revenue loss and reputational impact. Structurally acute because the Company supplies regulated markets under USFDA DMFs and EDQM CEPs from USFDA-audited and EUGMP-approved units, so a quality failure has market-access consequences. Product Quality is also flagged as a Governance RISK material topic. Mitigation: robust quality management systems, regular audits, process controls, employee training and continuous improvement, supported by TrackWise, LIMS and SAP.
- Environmental compliance — effluent, emissions and hazardous waste — Air Emissions, GHG Emissions, Hazardous Waste Management and Waste Water Treatment are all classified as Environmental RISK material topics. The BRSR materiality table identifies 'effluent generation from process having potential of water pollution and soil pollution' as the lead issue, and the LCA risk table adds 'social risks involve health and safety impacts on employees and local communities'. Structurally relevant because operations are chemistry-intensive and concentrated at one site. Mitigation: 100% Zero Liquid Discharge process treating, recycling and reusing water; ISO 14001:2015 audited by BSI; biofuel use in the captive power plant; Continuous Air Quality Monitoring System (CAQMS); authorised disposal and recycling channels. Note that BRSR discloses total waste generated rising to 8,693.23 MT in FY26 from 4,394.98 MT in FY25, with 'other hazardous waste' at 6,670.12 MT vs 2,705.21 MT, and Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions both rising, alongside the production expansion.
- Foreign exchange exposure — Named as the Financial risk category: 'Fluctuations in exchange rates impacting imports and export realisations', with impact of margin pressure, cost escalation and volatility in earnings. Structurally relevant given exports are 24% of total turnover across 70 international countries. Mitigation: continuous monitoring of currency exposure, hedging strategies and periodic market reviews.
- Cyber attack / information security and data privacy — Named as an Operational risk driven by increasing digitalisation, evolving cyber threats and unauthorised access attempts, with impact spanning operational disruptions, data breaches, regulatory non-compliance, financial losses and reputational damage; Data Privacy, Information Security and Counterfeit Risk are separately classified as Governance RISK material topics. Mitigation: comprehensive cybersecurity and IT governance frameworks, regular Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT), continuous monitoring and preventive controls; the Company is certified to ISO 27001.
- Innovation / R&D under-investment and business continuity — Innovation and R&D Risk is flagged: insufficient investment in R&D, technology and talent development would lead to reduced product innovation, slower new product development and loss of competitive advantage — material given nine molecules are in development and the diversification strategy depends on new commercialisations. Business Continuity Disruption is separately flagged (unforeseen events affecting critical operations, leading to operational interruptions, delayed deliveries, revenue loss and stakeholder dissatisfaction), mitigated by an established Business Continuity Plan, defined recovery protocols and periodic Business Impact Analysis reviews. Ethical Conduct & Monitoring is a further named risk, mitigated by internal controls, whistle-blower mechanisms and periodic compliance reviews.

business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Established in 1986, IOL operates through two primary business segments: Pharmaceuticals and Specialty Chemicals. The pharmaceutical business develops and manufactures a diversified portfolio of APIs spanning multiple therapeutic categories used in essential medicines, while the specialty chemicals business (established 1996) manufactures products such as Ethyl Acetate, Acetic Anhydride and Triacetin for a wide range of industrial applications, serving both captive requirements and merchant sales. Manufacturing is fully backward integrated, which the company says strengthens efficiency, product quality, supply reliability and cost competitiveness across regulated and semi-regulated markets.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Strengthen the manufacturing and integration platform — described as a strategic priority; during FY26 the Company strengthened manufacturing capabilities through strategic capacity expansions and investments in manufacturing facilities that support backward integration and supply chain reliability
- Build a broader and more diversified API business capable of delivering sustained growth across markets, reducing dependence on Ibuprofen
- Deepen backward integration to retain value in-house, improve supply assurance and sustain a structural cost advantage
- Expand presence in regulated markets through new product registrations, regulatory filings, approvals and deeper customer engagement
- Innovation and R&D as a growth pillar — build a pipeline of differentiated, value-added products through investments in R&D, process excellence and sustainable technologies; research focused on green chemistry, process innovation, cost-efficient synthesis and backward integration
- Leverage digital technologies and data-driven decision-making to improve operational efficiency, strengthen governance and enhance customer responsiveness
- Disciplined capital allocation, prudent risk management and responsible growth in executing the long-term strategic roadmap, with capital expenditure funded predominantly through internal accruals
- Prepare for the next phase of growth from the newly acquired 101-acre land parcel, with environmental, industrial and infrastructure approvals in progress and multiple opportunities under evaluation
- Sustainability embedded in strategy — measurable ESG targets, renewable energy adoption, 100% ZLD and water neutrality, and a long-term carbon-neutrality roadmap
- Long-term (5-10 year) growth pillars named in the Growth Strategy spread: Market Leadership in APIs and Specialty Chemicals; Innovation and New Product Development; Global Supply Chain Resilience; Digital Transformation and Technology Upgrades; Sustainability and Environmental Stewardship (the detail table for these pillars is truncated in the routed text)
- The Board states a philosophy of disciplined, prudent capital allocation with reinvestment prioritised over distribution. Its stated responsibilities expressly include reviewing capital allocation decisions, and the year's focus areas included capital efficiency and long-term value creation. On distribution, the Company has a Board-adopted Dividend Distribution Policy under Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations (published on the Company website), under which an interim dividend was declared for FY 2025-26 and treated as the final dividend for the year. On retention, the Board explicitly chose to retain the entire profits of FY 2025-26 in the Statement of Profit and Loss, transferring no amount to the General Reserve, 'in view of the Company's growth plans, capital expenditure requirements and strengthening the financial position of the Company'. Growth capital expenditure is stated to be funded predominantly (in the MD&A, entirely) through internal accruals, consistent with a near debt-free balance sheet and a reaffirmed CARE A+ (Stable) long-term / CARE A1+ short-term credit rating. The Company has not accepted any public or member deposits, has not granted stock options to its directors (including Independent Directors), and did not advance any loan to directors during the year other than advances for travel or official duties in the normal course. Independent Directors are paid sitting fees only, with no other remuneration; executive directors' remuneration components are all fixed with no severance fees payable. The Board also treats succession planning for Directors, KMP and Senior Management as a governance priority, reviewed periodically by the Nomination and Remuneration Committee.
- Reduce combined Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions by 58.8% by 2033 and Scope 3 emissions by 35% by 2033; SBTi targets approved and validated (the Company also states it is planning to revalidate its SBTi targets and convert them into intensity-based targets because of business-model expansion)
- Advance towards carbon neutrality by 2050
- Achieved a 14.4% reduction in combined Scope 1, 2 and 3 GHG emission intensity in FY 2025-26 (including new expansions); net Scope 1+2 emissions intensity per tonne of production reduced by 8.8% excluding new plants. GHG emissions are third-party verified per GRI guidelines and ISO 14064-1
- Maintain 100% water neutrality and sustain 100% Zero Liquid Discharge status at the manufacturing facility; target a further 5% reduction in water consumption per KL per tonne of production; ground water intensity disclosed as 0.31-0.15 KL/ton of production
- Approximately 77-80% of energy consumption met through renewable sources; 1,187 KW of solar capacity installed (510 KW, 62.1 and 615 KW listed as installed to date) with a further 1.5 MW solar project under phase-wise implementation, plus expanding use of biofuels and other cleaner alternatives
- Life Cycle Assessment programme: cradle-to-gate LCAs completed for Ibuprofen (34.43% of turnover), Metformin (6.12%), Ethyl Acetate (33.66%) and Acetic Anhydride (5.38%), all conducted by an independent external agency with results published; commitment to extend LCA studies across the entire product portfolio by 2033
- Zero instances of environmental non-compliance during the year, and no operations/offices in or around ecologically sensitive areas; an environmental impact assessment for the Barnala chemicals and APIs expansion was conducted by an independent external agency with results in the public domain
- Safety targets of Zero Reportable Accidents, Zero Lost Time Injury Rate and Zero Lost Time Fatality Rate — not met in FY26 (1 employee fatality, 1 recordable injury, employee LTIFR 1.46 vs 0 in FY25); ISO 45001:2018 OHS system covers 100% of plants and offices
- External ESG recognition: EcoVadis Gold Medal (awarded July 2026, top 5% of companies assessed globally, upgraded from Silver), Responsible Care logo for three consecutive years, CDP Climate Change & Water Security and CDP Supplier Engagement ratings, SA 8000:2014 certification, ISO 14001, ISO 50001, ISO 27001 and ISO 37001; BRSR carries Reasonable Assurance from Intertek India Private Limited
- Social and human-capital commitments: maintain zero human rights violations; 100% of permanent and other-than-permanent employees covered by health and accident insurance; 100% PF/gratuity/ESI coverage; 100% return-to-work rate and 98.23% retention after parental leave; 93.89% of employees trained on health and safety and 97.44% on skill upgradation; 100% of employees received performance and career development reviews; well-being spend at 0.26% of total revenue (FY25: 0.30%); structured Grievance Redressal Mechanism with escalation and anti-retaliation protection
- Diversity remains a stated opportunity rather than an achievement: women are 3.23% of permanent employees (100 of 3,095), 12.5% of the Board (1 of 8) and 0% of the 2 Key Management Personnel reported in BRSR; permanent-employee turnover rate 16.10% in FY26 (female 19.10%) versus 14.90% in FY25
- Circularity and waste: waste-to-wealth initiative recovering by-products and converting them to saleable product (Ammonium Sulphate recovery giving a 126.07 tCO2e carbon offset), in-house green hydrogen introduction eliminating transportation emissions, vehicle-clubbing in downstream product distribution, and local sourcing / multimodal RM vehicle concept saving 103.09 tCO2e; supplier decarbonisation via capacity building under the 'PRAYAS' initiative, which also covers a Social Audit of Tier-1 suppliers
- Contributing to seven prioritised UN Sustainable Development Goals through participation in the UN Global Compact (the Corporate Overview elsewhere states 17 SDGs — the two statements in the report differ); CSR programmes aligned to the SDGs focus on education, healthcare, environmental sustainability, livelihood and community development, delivered through the Section 8 subsidiary IOL-Foundation
- Materiality process: a double-materiality assessment (impact materiality and financial materiality) completed in FY 2025-26 based on peer review per GRI requirements, with 34 material topics coded across E (12), S (11) and G (11); the report states four newly identified topics remain marked TBC pending final classification, of which three are visibly left unclassified ('--') in the routed table: E12 Biodiversity, S10 Employee Attraction/Retention and S11 Labor Practices
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: IOL operates from a single, fully integrated manufacturing complex at Barnala, Punjab, spanning 180+ acres, bringing API and specialty chemical production together at one location with shared utilities and comprehensive backward integration. The complex comprises 18 manufacturing units across the API and chemical divisions with a stated total installed capacity of 2,13,126 MTPA, including dedicated and multi-product facilities, regulatory-approved production blocks (USFDA-audited and EUGMP-approved units) and highly automated, DCS-based chemical plants. During FY 2025-26 the Company continued to invest in capacity expansion, automation and process optimisation, with ALL capital expenditure funded through internal accruals. Named expansion actions during the year: Ethyl Acetate capacity was enhanced from 1,00,000 MTPA to 1,20,000 MTPA at a capital expenditure of approximately Rs 4 crore; Acetic Anhydride capacity was increased from 25,000 MTPA to 32,000 MTPA at a capital expenditure of approximately Rs 5.71 crore; and Triacetin capacity (6,000 MTPA) was commissioned. On the pharmaceutical side, Unit 11, the dedicated fully backward-integrated Paracetamol facility of 10,800 MTPA, was commissioned and scaled, expanding manufacturing scale in the analgesics segment. Minoxidil was commercially launched during the year (Unit 9B, 120 MTP installed) and nine additional molecules remain under development. Backward integration extends to key starting materials, including in-house Iso Butyl Benzene (12,000 MTPA) for the Ibuprofen chain. An environmental impact assessment was undertaken for the 'Expansion of Chemicals and APIs production unit at Village & Post Fatehgarh Channa, Mansa Road, District Barnala', conducted by an independent external agency with results communicated in the public domain. Regulatory milestones supporting the expanded platform include a Certificate of GMP Compliance of Manufacturer from the National Institute of Pharmacy and Nutrition, Hungary, and EDQM Certificates of Suitability for Pantoprazole Sodium Sesquihydrate Process-III, Metformin Hydrochloride Process-II, Sitagliptin Phosphate Monohydrate, Minoxidil and Clopidogrel Besilate. NOTE ON TRUNCATION: the routed MD&A 'Specialty Chemicals Portfolio' paragraph breaks off mid-word ('broadens our reve'), and the routed BRSR extract ends mid-word ('Environ') in the environmental-impact-assessment table, so the closing detail of both is not available.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Long-term outlook for both pharmaceutical and specialty chemical industries described as encouraging, supported by increasing healthcare demand, expanding global manufacturing opportunities and India's strengthening role as supply chains diversify
- Specialty chemicals industry began showing signs of recovery following an extended period of inventory correction; management believes its integrated platform positions it to capitalise as global specialty chemical demand gradually recovers
- Healthy demand seen during FY26 in Paracetamol, Metformin, Pantoprazole, Clopidogrel, Fenofibrate and Levetiracetam, increasing the contribution of non-Ibuprofen products
- Scaling of the fully integrated Paracetamol facility (commissioned in the previous year) strengthened manufacturing capability, supply reliability and operational efficiencies
- Backward integration benefits — improved supply assurance, enhanced cost efficiencies and greater operational efficiency/resilience — described as increasingly evident during the year
- Headwinds acknowledged for FY26: geopolitical uncertainty, pricing pressure and evolving market dynamics
- Macro backdrop cited: global economy grew ~3.5% in CY2025 (advanced 1.9%, EMDEs 4.5%); IMF projects global GDP growth of 3.0% in CY2026 and 3.4% in CY2027
- Indian economy grew 7.6% in FY 2025-26 with PFCE +7.7% and GFCF +7.1%; repo rate cut by 100 bps to 5.25%; capacity utilisation improved to approximately 75-76%
- Union Budget 2026-27 public capex of approximately Rs 12.2 lakh crore (3.1% of GDP) and continued emphasis on manufacturing, infrastructure and export competitiveness expected to create a favourable operating environment for pharmaceutical and specialty chemical manufacturers such as IOL
- India-EU FTA cited as a positive — preferential market access for over 99% of Indian exports, expected to benefit Indian pharmaceutical exporters through improved market access and reduced trade barriers
- Global pharmaceutical sales estimated at approximately $1.7-1.8 trillion in CY2025 with industry growth of 6-7%; projected to reach approximately $1.8-1.9 trillion in CY2026
- Global generic formulations market projected to grow at a CAGR of 5-6.5% to US$570-720 billion by the early 2030s, supported by patent expiries, affordability demand, chronic disease burden and biosimilar adoption
- Indian pharmaceutical industry valued at approximately US$65 billion in FY 2025-26, projected to reach US$130 billion by 2030 and approximately US$450 billion by 2047; India's share of the global pharmaceutical market projected to rise from ~3-3.5% to nearly 5% by 2030
- Indian pharma exports exceeded USD 30 billion in FY 2025-26, up 5.6% YoY, to over 200 countries
- Sector risks flagged in the industry narrative: pricing pressure in regulated markets, rising compliance costs, loss of exclusivity for key products, outcome-based pricing models, and intensifying generic/biosimilar competition
- Growth drivers named for Indian pharma: ageing population approaching 230 million by 2036, rising disposable income, increasing chronic disease burden, digitalisation of healthcare, and health insurance projected to grow at ~15% CAGR over the next five years (the 'Favourable Government' driver row is cut off mid-heading in the routed text)

deepdive.thesis: IOLCP delivered record Q4 revenue (INR 619cr, +17.4% YoY) and margin expansion (EBITDA 15.2%, +251bps) driven by near-maximum utilization in chemicals and recovering Ibuprofen demand, while guiding for sustained mid-to-high teen growth in FY27 supported by new Paracetamol capacity ramp-up and a massive INR 1,200-1,400cr greenfield project over 4-5 years.

open.item: Punjab-floods fuel-cost impact (~Rs 7-8 crore, ~1% margin) expected to normalize in Q3, reducing power cost by Rs 5-6 crore.
Management expects chemical-segment EBITDA margin of 5% to 6% for FY26.
Newly acquired 101-acre site to take 6-8 quarters for regulatory approvals; commercialization not expected until after FY26.

Management is hopeful of securing most of the remaining regulatory approvals for the greenfield site within the next three to four months, after which work will start there (environmental clearance already in place).
Company applied for environmental approvals for the new Chandigarh-Bathinda land and hopes to ramp up the facility in 18 to 24 months.
Management targets 40-45% export share for the company as a whole over the next two years, focused on European market.
Management guides for mid-teen to high-teen (around 15%, +/- 1-2%) revenue growth in FY27 versus FY26.
Management guides for FY27 blended EBITDA margin of around 14% to 14.5%, up from 12.4% in FY26.
Company targets increasing its non-ibuprofen export/regulated-market share to around 25% in FY2027 (from ~20% currently).
Paracetamol utilization on the enhanced 10,800 MT capacity (currently 55%) is expected to rise to around 70-75% in FY27 and reach full utilization by FY28.
Management is targeting around INR2,700 crore revenue in FY27 with roughly 15% annual top-line growth.
Management targets FY27 revenue of Rs 2,600-2,700 crore with EBITDA margin of 13-15%, expecting 10-15% revenue growth and 1-2% margin improvement each year.
Management aims to scale total export revenue from ~27% to about 40% (stated elsewhere 40-45%) over the medium term / next 2 years.
Management targets increasing export to 40% of total revenue (company-wide, chemical+pharma) in the coming two years (currently ~25%).
Management targets Rs 2,000 crore combined from Ibuprofen and non-Ibuprofen segments in the next two years.
Non-ibuprofen segment revenue targeted to roughly double from ~Rs 500 crore to Rs 800-1,000 crore in two-three years.
Management targets ~50% export realization from the non-ibuprofen segment within the next 2-3 years (currently ~23-24%).
Non-commodity APIs Clopidogrel, Pantoprazole and Fenofibrate each have potential of around INR100 crore to INR150 crore in the upcoming two years.
Management aims to raise total export share from ~30% to 45-50%, especially into regulated markets, over 3-4 years.
Management targets Rs 3,000 crore topline by FY28 from existing products, growing ~12-13% every year.
